one-line thesis: Pitti Engineering is transitioning from a commodity lamination vendor to an integrated solutions provider, driven by high-margin data center and railway export opportunities. The announced INR 290 Cr greenfield casting capex targets doubling capacity by FY30 to capture mining and locomotive demand, though near-term Q4/FY27 growth is tempered by West Asia energy disruptions and working capital normalization.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 506 Cr (Q4, +7% YoY), INR 1,953 Cr (FY26, +12% YoY). EBITDA: INR 326 Cr (FY26, +20% YoY), Margin 17% (up from 15.9%). PAT: Not explicitly broken out in transcript text, but tax INR 128 Cr. Order Book: Healthy pipeline cited, specific value not disclosed; volumes targeted 78k tons (lam) and 16k tons (machine) for FY27. Net Debt: ~INR 570 Cr (current), expected to reduce to ~INR 470 Cr post WC release, then ~INR 250 Cr by FY28 absent new capex. One-offs: Q4 margins impacted by sudden LPG/energy cost spike (West Asia crisis) and shipping constraints delaying ~INR 20 Cr exports; Forex losses on open contracts moved to OCI.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Targeting ~INR 2,300 Cr for FY27 (implied ~18% growth). Margins: Expecting similar % margins (17% range) subject to commodity pass-through; per-ton EBITDA stable. Order Inflow: Strong visibility in mining, locomotive, data centers. Capex/Commissioning: INR 290 Cr greenfield (Hyderabad) for casting/machining; commissioning Q1 FY30 (casting) and modular from FY28 (machining). Previous INR 150 Cr capex mostly done, remaining INR 50 Cr by H1 FY27.
order book & pipeline: Management cites 'healthy order pipeline' and 'strong growth' from marquee clients (Progress Rail, Siemens, Caterpillar, Wabtec) but does not disclose a specific monetary order book value. Volume guidance implies robust demand: Laminations target 78,000 tons (vs 69,500 in FY26); Machine components target 16,000 tons (vs 12,012 in FY26).
segment / subsidiary detail: FY26 Revenue Mix: Traction/Railway 33% (key focus, export heavy); Power Gen 15%; Industrial/Commercial Motors 13%; Special Purpose Motors 7%; Mining/Oil & Gas 6%; Renewables 3%; Data Centers 3% (fastest growing mid-term); Others 19%. Q4 Volume: 18,400 tons (lam/assemblies, +7.3% YoY); 2,783 tons (casting/machining, temporary softness). FY26 Volume: 69,500 tons (lam, +10%); 12,012 tons (casting, +15.4%). High value-added assemblies growing faster than loose laminations.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Data Centers: New applications in generator housing and turbine engine parts for US/Global clients; progression from loose laminations to high-value assemblies. 2) Mining/Off-Highway: Greenfield capex specifically targeting larger castings (up to 4 tons) for mining clients like Caterpillar. 3) Railway Exports: Diversification beyond domestic Indian Railways to global metro/loco projects (Siemens, Wabtec, Alstom, Progress Rail) mitigating domestic capex moderation. 4) Vertical Integration: Capturing margin from raw casting -> machining -> integrated assembly.
margins & cost dynamics: Margin Profile (EBITDA/ton): Raw Casting INR 30k-35k; Machined Casting INR 80k-100k; Loose Lamination INR 15k-18k; High Value-Added Assemblies INR 30k-60k. Cost Headwinds: Q4 saw sharp LPG/energy cost spikes due to West Asia tensions; mechanism is quarterly price pass-through, creating a lag impact. Forex: Quarterly price adjustment mechanism neutralizes currency fluctuation impact on margins, though depreciation aids competitiveness in bidding.
capex / expansion: Total Announced: INR 290 Cr (New Greenfield, Hyderabad) + INR 50 Cr (Pending previous). Breakdown: 30% Land/Civil, 70% Plant & Machinery. Focus: Doubling casting capacity to 36,000 MT (from ~18k effective); increasing machine hours from 7.2L to 10.8L. Timeline: Casting operational Q1 FY30; Machining modular commissioning starting FY28. Funding: INR 100 Cr from internal accruals, balance via debt. Asset Turn target: 1.2x.
capital allocation: Strategy: 1) Debottleneck existing lines; 2) Expand where visibility is strong (Mining/Data Center); 3) Build integrated platform. Debt Plan: Net debt currently ~INR 570 Cr; expects reduction to ~INR 470 Cr via working capital release (INR 125 Cr payables increase), then further to ~INR 250 Cr by FY28 assuming no additional lamination capex. Subsidy: Maharashtra investment promotion subsidy eligible from FY27/FY28, optimizing claim over 7-9 years based on sales ramp.
risks & watch-items: 1) Geopolitical/Energy: West Asia instability causing LPG shortages and freight disruptions (impacted Q4 exports by ~INR 20 Cr). 2) Working Capital: High inventory levels (~INR 400 Cr) and net working capital cycle (90-120 days for new projects) straining cash flows. 3) Execution: Greenfield commissioning delayed beyond FY30 could miss demand window. 4) Tax: Effective tax rate elevated (~33%) due to ESOP accounting and depreciation differences, persisting for few years.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural shift to value-added products and India's role in global supply chains; cautious on near-term Q1 FY27 due to lingering energy/logistics normalization; transparent about margin mechanics (per-ton vs %) and debt trajectory.
non-obvious takeaways: 1) Margin Lag: The quarterly price adjustment mechanism means sudden mid-quarter energy spikes (like Q4) cannot be passed through immediately, temporarily crushing margins until the next quarter's pricing resets. 2) Inventory Strategy: Management is intentionally holding high inventory (~INR 400 Cr) as a buffer against supply chain volatility, planning to draw this down in FY27 to release working capital and reduce debt. 3) Data Center Entry: Initially supplying loose laminations to US clients, with a structured 2-step plan to migrate them to high-value assembled stators/rotors from India once relationships mature.

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Bearings & motion-control localization
themes.need: Bearings and motion-control makers (MNC subs + domestic) ride an auto + industrial-aftermarket localization driver across automotive, railway, wind, off-highway and power-gen - distinct from machine-tool/process-equipment capex or pure OEM demand.
themes.driver: Auto + industrial/railway/wind/off-highway aftermarket localization and import-substitution.
